Hon'ble Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.
Hon'ble Prashant Kumar,J.
1.

Heard Sri Manvendra Nath Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Rajeev Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State-respondents and Sri Pranjal Mehrotra, learned counsel for the respondent No.4.
2.

The instant writ petition is preferred for a direction commanding Respondent No.3/Prescribed Authority/Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition), Gautam Buddh Nagar, to make payment of the compensation amount to the petitioner in compliance with the order dated 16.05.2018, passed by the Court of Arbitrator/District Magistrate, Gautam Buddha Nagar in Arbitration Case No.31 of 2016 under Section 3-G (7) of the Indian National Highway Act, 1956, and Munidraj vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102058447/

sentences.text: to ensure interest until the actual date of payment.

Alternatively, it is also prayed for a direction commanding Respondent No.3/Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition), Gautam Buddh Nagar, to consider and decide the petitioner's application dated 28.11.2023 by a reasoned and speaking order.
3. The instant matter relates to the disputed Khata No. 61, Khasra No. 858-Ga, admeasuring 0.7520 hectares, situated in Village Kot, Tehsil Dadri, District Gautam Buddha Nagar.

The land was recorded in the name of the petitioner's father, Kishan Lal S/o Ram Asrey, and during his lifetime,
the land was acquired by the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) on 05.02.2007, for the construction of the Eastern Peripheral Expressway, as per a Gazette notification issued under Section 3(2) of the National Highway Act, 1956 (in short 'Act, 1956').

It is claimed that an award was made, and the compensation for the acquired land was initially fixed at Rs.850/- per square meter,
as determined by the Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition) on 22.06.2009.

However,
this compensation amount was contested by the farmers of the area, including the petitioner, who filed objections and arbitration cases, including the aforesaid Arbitration Case No. 31 of 2016, under Section 3-G(7) of the Act, 1956, before the District Magistrate of Gautam Buddha Nagar.

entities.text: District Magistrate of Gautam Buddha Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: After considering the facts and evidence, the Arbitrator enhanced the compensation to Rs.3,500/- per square meter through an award dated 16.05.2018.

Learned counsel for the petitioner states that despite this clear-cut award, which has not been challenged or overturned by any court, the petitioner has not received any compensation for the acquired land.

Based on a supplementary affidavit, it is claimed that the petitioner's father, Kishan Lal, was the recorded tenure-holder of the aforesaid disputed Plot No. 858-Ga, as evidenced by CH Form 45 (Annexure SA-1 to the supplementary affidavit).

After the death of the petitioner's father, the land was inherited by the petitioner and his brothers, each owning one-third, amounting to 0.2523 hectares each, and his name was also mutated in the revenue records.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further states that the instructions provided by the authority, which were relied upon by the learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel, are per se incorrect, as the petitioner's father was the recorded tenure-holder, as reflected in the primary inquiry made by the NHAI.

He submits that the petitioner submitted an application on 28.11.2023 before the Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition) for the disbursement of compensation as per the Arbitrator's order, but no payment has been made till date.
A report from the Tehsil Authority dated 28.02.2024 confirms that the petitioner is the legal owner of 0.2523 hectares of the disputed land.

Despite repeated representations to the respondents,
no action has been taken, and the petitioner has become landless and is facing severe hardship due to the non-payment of compensation.

He submits that a direction be issued to Respondent No.3 /
Prescribed Authority/Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition), Gautam Buddh Nagar, to pay the compensation with interest as per the Arbitrator?s award dated 16.05.2018 within a stipulated period.
4. Considering the factual situation, we are not inclined to keep the writ petition pending consideration.

We dispose of the instant writ petition with an observation that Respondent No.3 /
Prescribed Authority/Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition), Gautam Buddh Nagar, may decide the claim of the petitioner in accordance with the law within two months from the date of production of a certified copy of this order, but certainly after providing an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and other necessary parties.
